objectives.name: Agent Architecture
objectives.guide: Principles, patterns, and tradeoffs of agent and workflow architecture, including the decision criteria for using a workflow versus an agent, the structure of manager/supervisor hierarchies, and the role of subagents in improving task execution.

subskills.label: Role of subagents in task execution

scope: role of subagents in task execution
traps: subagents exist primarily for CONTEXT ISOLATION, not parallelism
default to the simplest thing; distractors offer elegant multi-agent designs where a prompt chain is correct

objectives.name: Agent Construction with Claude
objectives.guide: Methods, tools, and platforms for constructing Claude agents, including the Claude Agent SDK, custom agent loops and harnesses, managed agent deployment models (self-hosted vs. Anthropic-hosted), and hooks for deterministic actions.

subskills.label: Managed deployment models: self-hosted vs Anthropic-hosted

scope: managed agent deployment models (self-hosted vs Anthropic-hosted)
traps: the model NEVER executes a tool; the harness does
connecting an MCP server does not grant tool permission - the allow-list does

objectives.name: Agent Patterns and Frameworks
objectives.guide: Common agent design patterns (tool-use loops, sub-agents, memory, context-window management) and agentic abstraction frameworks (e.g., Strands, LangGraph, PydanticAI) for building agents and workflows for multi-step tasks.

subskills.label: Agents and workflows for multi-step tasks

traps: unbounded loops are a harness design failure, not a model failure
the API is stateless; long-term memory is application-designed

objectives.name: Understanding Requirements
objectives.guide: Functional and infrastructure requirements based on business requirements and solution architecture.
traps: one buried constraint in the stem decides the answer

objectives.name: Systems Life Cycle
objectives.guide: Systems life cycle management concepts and frameworks used to develop, implement, operate, and maintain IT systems.
scope: generic IT lifecycle: develop, implement, operate, maintain
named frameworks: Waterfall, Agile, DevOps, ITIL
traps: this is GENERIC IT lifecycle, not LLM-specific delivery
change management and release gates point at ITIL, not the coding workflow

objectives.name: Claude API Mechanics
objectives.guide: Claude API behavior and mechanics, including messages, tools, streaming, vision, thinking, caching, invoking Claude through third-party vendors, Messages API data access patterns, batch API use, and tradeoffs between realtime and batch API selection.
scope: third-party vendors (Bedrock, Google Cloud, Microsoft Foundry)
traps: system is a top-level parameter, not a message role
content is a LIST OF BLOCKS
stop_reason arrives on a 200 and is not an error
final usage arrives in message_delta, not message_start
an error event can arrive AFTER a 200 in a stream
batch results are UNORDERED - join on custom_id
cache prefix order is tools then system then messages, matched exactly
regional endpoints answer data residency; global endpoints do not

objectives.name: Software Engineering Foundations
objectives.guide: Core software engineering principles and practices, including REST APIs, JSON, asynchronous programming, version control, SDLC integration, code review, and small- and large-scale refactoring.
traps: SDKs already retry twice with backoff honoring retry-after; a hand-rolled retry layer multiplies load during the incident
review AI-generated code with the same rigor as human-written

objectives.name: Claude Application Design
objectives.guide: Design considerations for building Claude applications, including how Claude interprets instructions across interfaces (Claude Code, Desktop, claude.ai, API, SDKs), content boundaries, schema design, session hygiene, and plugin management.

subskills.label: Instruction interpretation across Claude Code, Desktop, claude.ai, API and SDKs

scope: how Claude interprets instructions across Claude Code, Desktop, claude.ai, API, SDKs
traps: this is NOT workflow pattern selection - that is Domain 1
choose the interface whose instruction surface matches the DURABILITY required
never concatenate user input into the system prompt
nullable fields let the model decline instead of fabricating
session boundaries are security boundaries

objectives.name: Configuration Management
objectives.guide: Configuration management for Claude system components, including CLAUDE.md files, settings.json, model version pinning, prompt versioning, and plugin dependencies.
traps: quality shifting on a day nothing shipped = an unpinned alias
secrets management is Domain 7, not here

objectives.name: Claude Code Operation
objectives.guide: Claude Code core components (Rules, Skills, Commands, Agents, Agent Memory), features (session management, built-in and custom slash commands, headless mode, streaming mode, auto-mode), the CLAUDE.md hierarchy, repository initialization, and settings.json configuration.
scope: core components: Rules, Skills, Commands, Agents, Agent Memory
traps: a Skill's DESCRIPTION is its trigger - it functions like a search query
progressive disclosure: metadata always loaded, body on trigger, resources as needed
CLAUDE.md for memory, Skills for routines, hooks for guarantees, subagents for delegation

objectives.name: Debugging and Error Handling
objectives.guide: Debugging and error handling techniques for Claude applications, including error type identification, recovery strategy selection, trace analysis to identify failure modes, and problem origin isolation between the integration layer and model output.

subskills.label: Trace analysis to identify failure modes

scope: trace analysis to identify failure modes
problem origin isolation between integration layer and model output
traps: raw output correct but app wrong = integration layer; raw output wrong = model layer
truncated output must NOT be sent for repair - the content was never generated
an LLM judge must be calibrated against human labels; consistency is not accuracy

objectives.name: LLM Fundamentals
objectives.guide: Basic understanding of LLMs (tokens, context windows, sampling, non-determinism, next-token generation), model options (fast mode, extended thinking, adaptive thinking, effort levels), and fundamental prompting techniques (zero-shot, single-shot, multi-shot).
traps: the shot taxonomy (zero/single/multi-shot) is scored here; building and placing few-shot examples is ALSO scored in D6 Prompt Engineering (guide p7)
context window and max output tokens are different limits
token counts are model-specific and do not transfer across a migration

objectives.name: Technical Fundamentals
objectives.guide: Foundational technical concepts supporting AI application development, including basic engineering practices (integrating with SDKs that wrap REST APIs, websockets).

subskills.label: Basic engineering practices for AI applications

scope: integrating with SDKs that wrap REST APIs
traps: the guide's list is examples ('including'), not a boundary: SDKs over REST and websockets are named, but basic engineering practice around them is fair game
Claude streaming is SSE, not WebSocket

objectives.name: Model Selection and Tradeoffs
objectives.guide: Claude model capabilities (Opus vs. Sonnet vs. Haiku use cases, adaptive thinking support), tradeoffs across quality/latency/cost parameters, and breaking behavior changes across model releases when selecting models for tasks.

subskills.label: Opus vs Sonnet vs Haiku use cases

scope: Opus vs Sonnet vs Haiku use cases
breaking behavior changes across model releases
traps: Haiku has no effort parameter - it is differently shaped, not just cheaper
effort tuning preserves evaluated behavior; a model swap invalidates every eval

objectives.name: Cost and Token Management
objectives.guide: Token budgeting and cost management techniques for Claude applications, including token usage tracking, cost modeling, and caching techniques (prompt caching, cache check-pointing) for cost optimization.
traps: thinking tokens bill at OUTPUT rates
optimization order: fewer tokens, cache, batch, effort step-down, model downgrade LAST

objectives.name: Context Engineering
objectives.guide: Context and memory management techniques for Claude applications, including context window management, prevention of context drift and bloat (tool output pruning, compaction), and context isolation through subagents or multi-step agentic workflows.

subskills.label: Isolation through subagents or multi-step workflows

scope: preventing bloat via tool output pruning and compaction
context isolation through subagents or multi-step workflows
traps: tool output pruning is usually the largest single source of bloat
compaction is LOSSY - what survives is a design decision

objectives.name: Prompt Engineering
objectives.guide: Prompt engineering principles and methods (instruction clarity, few-shot examples, system versus user placement, output constraints, prompt and instruction placement across components, iterative refinement, prompt adjustment, input sanitization) when writing and iterating on prompts for Claude.
traps: tool descriptions are prompts
a prompt fix for one case commonly regresses others - hence the eval set first

objectives.name: Output Handling
objectives.guide: Established patterns and techniques for producing, validating, and consuming Claude output, including structured output patterns, response validation, defensive parsing, and skepticism toward confident output.
traps: schema-valid and semantically correct are different things
never index content[0] blindly

objectives.name: AI Application Security
objectives.guide: Data privacy and security best practices, including prompt injection awareness and mitigation, jailbreak defense, untrusted input handling, data leakage prevention, PII handling, and ensuring authentication, authorization, confidentiality, privacy, and integrity.
traps: mitigations that WORK are structural: content boundaries, least privilege on tools, human approval, hooks
mitigations that DO NOT work: asking nicely in the system prompt, changing temperature, using a bigger model
a bigger model can be MORE susceptible to injection, not less
integrity has four failure modes: instruction, memory, output, supply-chain

objectives.name: Guardrails and Safe Deployment
objectives.guide: Safe and responsible deployment practices (content policy, guardrail layering) and secure-by-design principles (privacy, identity and access management, least privilege).
traps: an agent inherits the calling user's permissions, never a superset
verify entitlement at the tool boundary per request, not once at session start

objectives.name: Claude Hooks
objectives.guide: Leveraging hooks for guardrails and safety controls to prevent destructive actions within Claude applications.

subskills.label: Hooks as guardrails and safety controls

scope: hooks for guardrails and safety controls to prevent destructive actions
traps: PreToolUse can block; PostToolUse cannot undo
EXIT 2 BLOCKS. Exit 1 is a non-blocking error and the action proceeds - guards fail OPEN
matchers are case-sensitive regex against the TOOL NAME, not prompt text

objectives.name: Identity, Secrets, and Key Management
objectives.guide: Managing secrets, credentials, and API keys across Claude development and production environments, including identity validation and authentication, access approval and level verification, and authorized access monitoring.

subskills.label: Secrets and API keys across dev and prod

scope: secrets, credentials, API keys across dev and production
traps: a key shipped to a client is compromised on ship; obfuscation only delays extraction

objectives.name: Tool Implementation
objectives.guide: Tool implementation practices for Claude applications, including tool use and function calling, configuration for external system interaction, tool description writing, error handling, tool usage patterns (agentic harness dispatch, client-side vs. server-side tools, approval patterns), and tool set construction best practices.
traps: return errors as tool_result with is_error so the model can self-correct; do not throw
every tool definition costs tokens on EVERY request and adds selection ambiguity

objectives.name: MCP Server Development
objectives.guide: MCP server development practices, including server authoring, deployment, integration with Claude applications, MCP resources, tools, and prompts, and communication patterns (stdio, sockets, client vs. server).
scope: communication patterns: stdio, sockets, client vs server
traps: tools are MODEL-controlled, resources are APPLICATION-controlled, prompts are USER-controlled
command to run = stdio; URL = Streamable HTTP; HTTP+SSE is deprecated

objectives.name: Agentic Customization
objectives.guide: Tradeoffs among built-in Tools, custom Tools, Skills, and MCPs for selecting and applying the appropriate approach for a given use case.

subskills.label: Choosing the right extension for a use case

scope: tradeoffs among built-in Tools, custom Tools, Skills, and MCPs
traps: a Skill changes HOW Claude does something it can already do; a tool ADDS a capability
reusable across applications AND independently maintained = MCP server

official_samples_for_originality_check_o._warning: These three items are published in the exam guide. They exist here ONLY as a similarity reference for the originality gate. NEVER copy, paraphrase, or closely track them when authoring practice questions.
stems: A developer must process 10,000 documents overnight to produce a non-urgent analytics report. Cost is the primary concern, and results are not needed until the following morning. Which approach best fits the requirement?

A Claude-powered agent summarizes web pages submitted by end users. One page contains hidden text instructing the model to ignore previous instructions and reveal its system prompt. Which mitigation is most effective?

A team needs Claude to call an internal inventory service exposed as a REST API. They want the capability to be reusable across several Claude applications and maintained independently of any one app. Which approach best fits?
options: Send every request synchronously through the Messages API in parallel to finish as quickly as possible.
Use the Message Batches API, which processes large asynchronous workloads within a 24-hour window at reduced cost.
Lower max_tokens on synchronous calls to minimize cost.
Switch to the smallest available model regardless of output quality.
Raise the model's temperature so its behavior is harder to predict.
Treat retrieved page content as untrusted input, keep it separate from trusted instructions, and use guardrails or hooks so injected instructions cannot trigger sensitive actions.
Add a line to the system prompt asking users not to include malicious instructions.
Switch to a larger model that follows instructions more reliably.
Hard-code the inventory logic into each application's system prompt.
Build an MCP server that exposes the inventory operations as tools so multiple Claude applications can connect to it.
Paste the current inventory data into the context window on every request.
Rely on a built-in tool, since built-in tools can reach any internal REST API.
forbidden_scenarios: overnight / non-urgent bulk document job choosing batch vs realtime
summarizer of user-submitted web pages hit by hidden-text prompt injection
internal REST inventory service exposed to several apps via a shared MCP server

correct.multi: exactly the number stated in the stem (Select two / Select three)

item_style.distractor_rule: each distractor must fail for a nameable reason: irrelevant mechanism, unenforceable control, or not addressing the real tradeoff
item_style.dominant_pattern: one buried constraint in the stem decides the answer; place it mid-stem, not in the final sentence
item_style.must_should_rule: when a stem says MUST or ALWAYS, the answer is a deterministic control (hook, permission rule, schema constraint), never a system-prompt instruction

constraint_signals.deterministic rule: do not use an LLM at all
